title: Courses
summary: A course is a folder on one theme that lists lessons in order; it can be completed, mastered and closed.
description: A course gathers the lessons on one theme: a trip, a hobby, the learner's work. It holds no words of its own and reaches them only through the lessons it lists.

stories.as: a learner with a trip, a hobby or a job that needs Polish
stories.want: a course on that theme with its lessons in order
stories.soThat: I can work through it from start to finish

stories.as: a learner who has mastered a course
stories.want: to close it as a trophy

requirements.text: A course lists its lessons in an order that the tutor can change.
Words given to a course are cut into word drills of at most 8, and sentences into sentence drills of at most 5.
Dialogue lines given to a course join its conversation lesson, or start one if it has none.
Words and sentences a course already teaches are skipped when more is added to it, and the number skipped is reported.
A lesson can be listed in several courses; it keeps one schedule and one mastery, shown in each.

deprecation.reason: It can not, a lesson van be in a single course as that makes integrity easier.

requirements.text: A lesson can be moved from one course to another.

deprecation.reason: It can not. A new lesson can be created in the other course.

requirements.text: Taking a lesson out of its course deletes the lesson, with its words and their history.

history.text: Taking a lesson out of the last course that lists it deletes the lesson, with its words and their history.
history.reason: A lesson is in one course now, so its course is always its last.

requirements.text: Other lessons is a single folder at the bottom of the course list for lessons that fit no course; it can never be completed or closed.
A course is completed when every core lesson (every lesson that is not a challenge) has been passed once. A course of challenges only counts those as its core.
A course is mastered when it is completed and every lesson in it, challenges included, is mastered.
Reaching completed or mastered is celebrated once for each course.
Only a mastered course can be closed, by the learner's own choice; a closed course is listed under Mastered and can no longer be renamed, changed or added to. It can still be deleted.
A course can carry a CEFR level, stored apart from its title and shown as a badge.
A course without a level is given one only when the learner asks: the Exercises tab offers a button that asks the tutor.
A course's page lists its lessons, its words and its sentences, each item with the drill it belongs to.
A course can have a picture, drawn by an image model from its title, summary and words.
A new course should strive for diversity of lesson types
Every lesson is in exactly one course; Other lessons counts as one.
Upgrading takes a lesson listed in several courses off every course but the one it was first added to.
